findings.problem: This diff reverts commit e11187e ('fix: use preconfigured jinja2.Environment for autoescape'), whose message states verbatim: 'Starlette removed the **env_options passthrough in Jinja2Templates, breaking autoescape=True on newer versions.' That commit replaced `Jinja2Templates(directory=..., autoescape=True)` with an explicit `jinja2.Environment(loader=..., autoescape=True)` passed via `env=`, specifically because the `directory=` + `autoescape=True` kwarg form is documented (in starlette's own source) as deprecated: passing `autoescape` this way routes through `**env_options`, which starlette's Jinja2Templates.__init__ explicitly warns is being phased out ('Extra environment options are deprecated. Use a preconfigured jinja2.Environment instead.'). I ran the project's actual pinned environment (fastapi 0.133.0 / starlette 0.52.1, via `uv run`) and confirmed that *today* `templates.env.autoescape` still evaluates to True under the reverted form, so there is no live exploit in the current lockfile. However: (1) `pyproject.toml` pins no version bound at all for `fastapi` (`dependencies = ["fastapi", ...]`), so a future `uv lock --upgrade` can freely resolve a starlette release where the env_options passthrough is actually dropped; (2) there are no `| safe`/`Markup` usages anywhere in triggarr/templates/ acting as a secondary XSS guard, and no test in tests/ asserts `autoescape` is True, so a silent regression would ship undetected; (3) the only evidence that this specific break mode (silent accept-without-apply, not a hard TypeError) is the risk is the original author's own commit message, but that is first-party, specific evidence, not generic 'sensitive area' speculation. This is a protection being reverted back to a pattern the codebase's own history documents as broken, made fragile by an unpinned dependency.
findings.title: Revert of deliberate autoescape fix reintroduces version-fragile XSS protection
findings.why_it_matters: Autoescape is the only XSS defense in this codebase's templates (no `| safe` filters exist to audit individually). If a future starlette release stops honoring autoescape passed through the deprecated `**env_options` kwarg, every Jinja2 template in the app would render user- and config-influenced strings (instance names, search log entries, config values, error text) unescaped, turning every templated page into a stored/reflected XSS vector simultaneously, with no test to catch the regression before it ships.

agent_notes: Block shipping: the new constructor call breaks application startup with Starlette 1.0.

findings.fix_hint: Retain the explicit jinja2.Environment(autoescape=True) passed through env=, which both versions support, and verify application imports with Starlette 1.0.
findings.problem: Starlette 1.0 removed the autoescape constructor keyword, so this module-level call raises TypeError when routes are imported by triggarr/__main__.py, preventing startup. Dockerfile installs with `pip install .` without uv.lock, and pyproject.toml leaves FastAPI unconstrained; FastAPI supports Starlette 1.0+. The installed 0.52.1 still accepts the keyword and escapes correctly, masking the production compatibility failure. See the [Starlette constructor](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kludex/starlette/1.0.0/starlette/templating.py) and [FastAPI release notes](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/release-notes/#01330).
